crime: Every evening in the lounge, one girl opened her notebook and read aloud the stories the other prisoners had told her. She always kept the seat beside her free for {WITCH_NAME}, who never came.

One night, alone with her by the fountain in the courtyard, {WITCH_NAME} told her a story of her own: she had once given her diary to her only friend to hide from her mother, and the friend had read it aloud to the whole class. "Please don't tell anyone," she said.
Then one evening the girl opened her notebook in the lounge and read that story to everyone. "So you'll stop hating her," she said. {WITCH_NAME} stood in the doorway and heard every word.

Before lockup, the prisoners at the upper railing saw the girl below, writing at the fountain as the snow came down. She waved them on to their cells. Just before the doors locked, {WITCH_NAME} pulled the half-open courtyard door shut behind the girl's back. Her touch sealed it; now no hand but hers could open it.
At six the next morning, walking to breakfast among the other girls, she brushed the door with a fingertip as she passed.
That morning they found the girl curled up under the tree by the fountain, frozen, her notebook in her lap. The courtyard door swung open at a push.
In the trial court, the prisoners agreed she had nodded off writing in the snow and frozen there. No door, as far as they could tell, had ever been shut on her.
But in the courtyard, one prisoner had turned the girl's hands over and found her fingernails torn. On the courtyard side of the door, just under the handle, were scratches to match.
The court understood then. A door that opened at any push had held all night against her clawing, as only a door shut by {WITCH_NAME} could.
fields.epitaph: Of everyone, she let only one girl in, and that was the girl she shut out.
execution: From the execution stand rises a notebook as tall as the trial court, lying open. She lies bound across its pages.
One by one, the pages lift and turn over onto her. Each settles across her face and chest, on top of the last.
She pushes at each page with her fingertips, trying to get it off her face, and each time the next comes down before she can.
The notebook lies open, its turned pages heaped flat over her. Only her fingertips show at the edge. They do not move.

magic.name: Her Hand Only
magic.text: She can seal any door, lid or clasp she closes so that only she can open it.
